about: Prompt tuning: the starting point for every prompt. soundlab/tuning.py documents the shape; AGENTS.md says how agents use it.

alerts.note: Earcon kits: the model makes single notes, alerts.py retunes and sequences them. Recordings: whole takes.

instruments.note: Solo auditions of the music's candidate instruments, one instrument each.

music.note: A spine from text, then the other levels derived from it with audio-to-audio (music.py).

taste.text: Music: the close profile is much better than contrast (levels that keep the spine's chords, with gentler contrast).

Emberhold's music: it's a medieval RTS of monsters and bloody warfare, so dark and martial, never pastoral or cosy folk. The calm tier must be more interesting (a brooding build-up between fights that still carries a theme, not ambient mush); raise the bar on all three tiers.

Emberhold's music: avoid folk music. No Folk/Nordic genre tags and no folk instruments carrying it (fiddles, lyre, kantele, frame drum, willow flute); the score is dark cinematic: string and brass sections, choirs, big drums, dread textures.

stable-audio-3-medium.name: Stable Audio 3 Medium
stable-audio-3-medium.summary: SoundLab's engine. Trained on Freesound and AudioSparx clips and their metadata, and run at cfg 1.0 with no negative prompt, so it follows literal descriptions and the training data's tags. Under 1 s per sound-effect take; about 12 GB of VRAM.

rules.text: Be explicit and concrete, one idea per prompt: name the physical source, the action, and how it was recorded.
rules.why: At cfg 1.0 it takes the words literally; a second idea blurs into the first.

rules.text: Use the training data's tags: TrackType: SFX for sound effects; TrackType: Music, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: …, Instruments: … for music; TrackType: Instrument for one instrument alone.
rules.why: The metadata it was trained on.

rules.text: No negations: "no music" or "without hiss" only adds the word. Say it positively (dry, close, clean).
rules.why: There's no negative prompt at cfg 1.0.

rules.text: No game lore: names like draugr or Mist-Walker mean nothing to it. Say what physically makes the sound.
No mixing-engineer adjective lists ("warm rounded attack, soft organic timbre…"): mastering handles tone, the prompt describes the sound.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: the project's own prompts with that tail (el) won 14% of sounds; the same descriptions without it (core) won 25%.

rules.text: Split multi-part sounds: "a body falls and a man groans" is two generations mixed, not one prompt.
Short and literal wins: about 18 words.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14, share of sounds won: core (~18 words) 25%, tags (~17) 20%, vivid (~42) 14%, el (~36) 14%, plain (~18) 13%, alt (a different source, ~29) 9%.

rules.text: Natural recordings (animals, crowds) are used whole: chopping and retuning them sounds artificial.
Pitch and rhythm can't be prompted exactly. For a motif, ask for one single note at a time; alerts.py retunes and sequences them and checks the pitch.
Give the tempo, the mode or key, the instruments, and one mood word. For a set that must mesh, one tempo and key everywhere.
Start music from the game's genre and stakes (the project's taste), then the level's mood: a context's mood word alone ("warm") pulls a war game toward pastoral folk.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: round 1's styles (story: "a quiet moment after the day's work", tune, saga, dance) were judged "the opposite direction" for a medieval RTS of monsters and warfare before any vote; dropped unvoted.

rules.text: Derived levels can't add intensity: audio-to-audio from the spine keeps its density at every strength, so calm, tension and action come out the same music at different volumes. Raising action's strength (0.65, 0.8) only loosens it (fewer onsets, less low end). Intensity has to be added another way (a layer over the level), and the spine must already carry a theme; never prompt calm as "sparse, lots of space".
rules.why: Emberhold 2026-10-14, round 3 (35 takes): at 0.5 the three levels matched within ~3% in onsets/s (11.8-14.3), punch (~7 dB crest) and energy under 150 Hz; action at 0.65/0.8: onsets/s down 0.5-1.7 in 3 of 4 styles, low end 0.16 -> 0.10. The designer: action "rarely intense enough", "always missing a layer, either a melody or intense rhythm".

rules.text: Instrument auditions: tags + one sentence ("TrackType: Instrument, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: …, Instruments: …. <who plays what>, 90 BPM, <key>, <room>.") wins for orchestral ensembles and choirs; SA3's own assistant shape ("TrackType: Instrument, <instrument> <style> motif loop with <character>. BPM: X.") wins for unusual sound-makers (bowed cymbal, bullroarer, bagpipes, throat singing). Leave out "Length: N seconds" (the assistant's UI strips it to set the duration). Voices work as a choir or chant: the model's assistant treats vocal words as failures, but the auditions found usable choirs.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: 13 dark candidates, each in both shapes with the same content, 4 seeds each; picks: tags 9 (malechoir, chant, strings, tremolo, horns, lowbrass, drumensemble, timpani, waterphone), guide 4 (bowedcymbal, bullroarer, sackpipa, throat). Picks only, no thumbs. Source of the assistant's shape: stable_audio_3/interface/reprompt.py.

rules.text: Music: name every part of the arrangement, as a film cue has them: the theme's instrument, a counter-line or ostinato, the bass, and the percussion section. Three parts (strings, brass, one drum) leave it thin.
rules.why: Emberhold 2026-10-14, round 3: 13 likes over 35 takes, the designer "kinda meh"; note on bloodmoon~war: "always missing a layer, either a melody or intense rhythm". Styles named 2-4 parts.

rules.text: Music in SA3's own prompt-assistant shape (one flowing sentence: "Dark cinematic war score in D aeolian with trombones playing a grim theme, low strings driving a dark ostinato and a drum ensemble pounding a heavy martial rhythm, creating ominous, dark tension. BPM: 90.") does at least as well as the tag shape, and made the designer's favourite. Genres that won: cinematic war, orchestral; choir and horror trailed.
rules.why: Emberhold 2026-10-14, round 3, likes per style (3 contexts, ~9 takes each): trailer 5 (incl. the favourite), war 5 (tags, same content), horror 2, choir 1. Choir also fails the beat check (day: 2 of 14 seeds passed).

rules.text: Off-sounding takes can be caught before the user hears them: Meta's Audiobox Aesthetics content enjoyment (CE) predicts the user's music likes; `music generate` rejects a take with a level under quality.GATE (calm 6.3, tension 6.8, action 6.3) and `music check` flags weak levels, long pauses, drift and noise on the Music page. Hand-made measures (key fit, sudden-change novelty) didn't predict likes; long pauses can be composed breaks.
rules.why: Emberhold 2026-10-14, round 3 (35 takes, 13 liked): CE on the spine AUC 0.82, calm 0.79; within choir and horror the liked takes were the top-rated; no liked take under 6.74 calm / 6.94 tension / 6.37 action, while 9 of 22 unliked were. Drift AUC 0.35, key ~0.5. Round 4's takes the designer called weird (bloodmoon~anthem k0, k1) rated 6.4-6.5 or had 7.7 s of calm dropouts.

templates.sfx: TrackType: SFX, {what physically makes it} {doing what, once}, {one detail of the action}, {close mic / distant}, {indoors / outdoors}.
templates.alerts: One single {low | high} note {plucked on | bowed on | struck on} {the instrument, plainly}. One note only. {its tone, in a few words}
templates.instruments: TrackType: Instrument, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: {genre}, Instruments: {instrument}. {what it plays, in one sentence}, {tempo} BPM, {key}, close mic, dry room.
templates.music: TrackType: Music, VocalType: Instrumental, Genre: {genre}, Genre: {genre}, Instruments: {instruments}. {mood}, {style}: {who plays what, plainly}, {tempo} BPM, {key or mode}, {meter}.

examples.prompt: TrackType: SFX, an axe striking a pine log, one crisp chop, close mic, outdoors.
examples.why: The shape to start from: source, action, recording.

examples.prompt: arrow impact, turf, ground, thock, single hit, short, solid, earthy, foley, close, clean, dry
examples.why: A Freesound-style tag caption; picked for arrow_hit.

examples.prompt: Cold wind howls and moans over bare rock on a high mountain pass at night, gusts whistling through crags and pebbles rattling.
examples.why: A plain description of what physically makes it; picked for amb_night_highlands.

examples.prompt: Two short, low calls on a wooden cow horn from the village, firm but warm and woody, a soft breathy attack, gentle outdoor air. Warm, mellow and rounded, smooth muted highs, gentle swell in and out, restrained dynamics, modest natural reverb, intimate rather than cinematic.
examples.why: The second half is a mixing-engineer tail: words, not sound.

examples.prompt: TrackType: Music, VocalType: Instrumental, Dark cinematic war score in D aeolian with trombones playing a grim theme, low strings driving a dark ostinato and a drum ensemble pounding a heavy martial rhythm, creating ominous, dark tension. BPM: 90.
examples.why: The spine of the designer's favourite ("by far my favorite so far", "bangs hard"), shipped 2026-10-14 as night.any.trailer.k2.close.

moss-soundeffect-v2.0.name: MOSS-SoundEffect v2.0
moss-soundeffect-v2.0.summary: A 1.3B diffusion transformer for sound effects, run outside SoundLab (its own runtime) and imported into the index. It takes a negative prompt beside the prompt. About 24 s per take here, against under 1 s for Stable Audio 3.

rules.text: It takes a negative prompt: put what to avoid there, and keep the prompt itself positive.
rules.why: The imported takes carry one, e.g. "piercing peaks, hiss, metallic ringing, cinematic boom".

rules.text: Prompts written for Stable Audio 3 don't carry over. Its own style still needs finding: start from short literal captions.
rules.why: Emberhold, 2026-10-14: fed the same prompts, moss-core won 1 of 7 sounds, moss-el and moss-vivid 0 of 7; 3 of 84 takes silent.
